## Context / Problem
Current recovery lives inside the facade and only repairs interrupted creates. A crash after the retired tombstone replacement but before the live replacement leaves the same exact identity live and retired. That partial state is detectable and safely completable, but construction-time or preview-time repair would violate read-only operations. The rich-text handler also still mutates an entry obtained from `all_bindings()`.

## Outcome
Extract incomplete-operation recovery behind the facade, cut the production rich-text caller to S2s narrow operation, and add journal-free interrupted-retirement completion at the validated write-bearing reconcile boundary. A durable tombstone is the authoritative retirement intent. Recovery removes the redundant live forward/reverse pair only when tombstone, forward, and reverse identities agree exactly; repeat is a no-op, and all ambiguity safety-aborts. Only explicit `unretire` removes that intent; a later automatic 200/`clear_absent`/same-key confirm does not implicitly resurrect a tombstoned identity.

## Plan
1. Move keyed/keyless create recovery into `binding_recovery.py` without changing label forms, immutable known-key handling, three-miss plus 3600-second conjunction, per-entry failure collection, or continue behavior.
2. Add a pure classifier for interrupted retirement states and a repository-backed completion operation. Require exact local id and Jira key agreement in tombstone, forward entry, and reverse entry.
3. Invoke completion after the immutable configuration operation snapshot, provider/config preflight, exclusive pass ownership, and under-lock staleness validation, but before any remote issue fetch, binding walk, differ, or lifecycle mutation in that pass. Load, construction, reconcile-check, dry-run, preview, selection, and filtered operations remain read-only.
4. Treat the tombstone as the committed side of the retired-first protocol. `absent_404_count`, a later 200, `clear_absent`, or same-key `bind_confirm` in a historical overlap is not a revocation signal; explicit `unretire` removes the tombstone, after which no completion candidate exists. If live replacement fails, retain the overlap and safety-abort for a later retry.
5. Replace `apply_handlers.py` mutation-through-`all_bindings()` with S2s facade operation after RP-04 S3 has landed its scoped-runtime changes to that file.
6. Finalize `docs/adr/0099-binding-store-internal-ownership.md` when the behavior lands: record tombstone authority versus explicit unretire, the before-observation repair boundary, intentional behavior change, rollback, and the explicit ban on broad tickets-branch staging.

## Dependencies / coordination
This story depends directly on RP-02 S1 and S2. Its `apply_handlers.py` and live-boundary edits must be rebased after RP-04 S3 (`talismanic-profitable-isopod`) closes. That cross-root execution condition is recorded as a soft relation because Rebars hierarchy resolver would otherwise promote a child edge into an unnecessarily broad RP-02-epic → RP-04-epic blocker; overlapping file impact remains visible.

## Testing (RED → GREEN)
- Fault-cut tests create the real retired-first/live-failed overlap, reopen a fresh store, execute pre-observation live recovery, and assert coherent retired-only bytes and repeat no-op.
- Mismatch tables vary each identity, missing reverse/live entries, corrupt live bytes, and replacement failure; the oracle is zero guessed deletion plus a typed safety abort.
- Intent-order tests cover a historical overlap whose stale live record was cleared/reconfirmed to the same key: the tombstone still completes. An explicit `unretire` removes the tombstone and prevents repair.
- Read-only surface tests spy on `os.replace`/repository save across construction, check, dry-run, preview, selection, and filter modes and assert zero calls.
- Existing create recovery/index-lag and rich-reemit suites remain exact behavior oracles.

## Compatibility / rollback
Disabling the pre-observation recovery call restores the prior detectable overlap; coherent stores are never rewritten. The public recovery method and failure tally remain compatible. Rollback of the rich-text call returns to the shallow query path without a format change. No journal, eager recovery, broad publication, automatic resurrection, or remote rollback is added.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given the real retired-first/live-replace fault cut, the next validated write-bearing pass completes repair before remote issue observation and retains the tombstone.
- [ ] Repeating completion is a no-op; any tombstone/forward/reverse mismatch, corrupt live file, or replace failure leaves recoverable evidence and safety-aborts without unrelated mutation.
- [ ] Construction, load, reconcile-check, dry-run, preview, selection, and filtered runs perform zero recovery writes.
- [ ] A later automatic 200/`clear_absent`/same-key confirm does not override a durable tombstone; explicit `unretire` removes the tombstone and prevents completion.
- [ ] Keyed pending recovery performs no search; keyless pending requires both three misses and 3600 seconds before unbind; per-entry failures remain loud and nonfatal to other entries.
- [ ] `apply_handlers.py` uses the narrow rich-emission facade and no production code mutates a binding through `all_bindings()`.
- [ ] ADR 0099 records the realized repair rule, pre-observation boundary, explicit-unretire reversal, rollback, and prohibition on broad tickets-branch staging.
